```{r Step 2: Initial Modeling on Relationship between Efficacy and Race, include=TRUE}
run_efficacy_simple <- function(data, outcome, race_group) {
  
  lapply(sort(unique(data$year)), function(y) {
    
    data_y <- data %>%
      filter(
        year == y,
        !is.na(.data[[outcome]]),
        !is.na(personal_finances_scale_factor),
        !is.na(VCF0009z)
      )
    
    if (nrow(data_y) == 0) return(NULL)
    
    design_y <- survey::svydesign(
      ids = ~1,
      weights = ~VCF0009z,
      data = data_y
    )
    
    mod <- survey::svyglm(
      as.formula(
        paste(
          outcome,
          "~ personal_finances_scale_factor"
        )
      ),
      design = design_y
    )
    
    list(
      year = y,
      race = race_group,
      outcome = outcome,
      n = nrow(data_y),
      model = mod
    )
  })
}


# Government care
```

```{r Step 3: Running the Model with Income, include=TRUE}
# Function to estimate the full three-way efficacy model
run_efficacy_full <- function(data, outcome, race_group) {
  
  lapply(sort(unique(data$year)), function(y) {
    
    data_y <- data %>%
      filter(
        year == y,
        !is.na(.data[[outcome]]),
        !is.na(personal_finances_scale_factor),
        !is.na(income_group_factor),
        !is.na(stock_owns),
        !is.na(VCF0009z)
      )
    
    if (nrow(data_y) == 0) return(NULL)
    
    design_y <- survey::svydesign(
      ids = ~1,
      weights = ~VCF0009z,
      data = data_y
    )
    
    mod <- survey::svyglm(
      as.formula(
        paste(
          outcome,
          "~ personal_finances_scale_factor *",
          "income_group_factor * stock_owns"
        )
      ),
      design = design_y
    )
    
    list(
      year = y,
      race = race_group,
      outcome = outcome,
      n = nrow(data_y),
      model = mod
    )
  })
}


# Government care
care_black_full <- run_efficacy_full(
  black_anes,
  "government_care",
  "Black"
)

care_white_full <- run_efficacy_full(
  white_anes,
  "government_care",
  "White"
)


# Government say

# Function to test the three-way interaction across all survey waves
run_threeway_tests <- function(model_list) {
  
  results <- lapply(model_list, function(x) {
    
    if (is.null(x)) return(NULL)
    
    test <- tryCatch(
      survey::regTermTest(
        x$model,
        ~ personal_finances_scale_factor:
          income_group_factor:
          stock_owns
      ),
      error = function(e) {
        return(e)
      }
    )
    
    # If the Wald test failed
    if (inherits(test, "error")) {
      
      return(
        data.frame(
          year = x$year,
          race = x$race,
          outcome = x$outcome,
          n = x$n,
          F = NA_real_,
          df_num = NA_real_,
          df_den = NA_real_,
          p_value = NA_real_,
          test_status = paste("FAILED:", test$message)
        )
      )
    }
    
    # Successful test
    data.frame(
      year = x$year,
      race = x$race,
      outcome = x$outcome,
      n = x$n,
      F = unname(test$Ftest),
      df_num = unname(test$df),
      df_den = unname(test$ddf),
      p_value = unname(test$p),
      test_status = "OK"
    )
  })
  
  dplyr::bind_rows(results)
}

# Run all four sets of tests
care_black_threeway <- run_threeway_tests(care_black_full)
care_white_threeway <- run_threeway_tests(care_white_full)

say_black_threeway <- run_threeway_tests(say_black_full)
say_white_threeway <- run_threeway_tests(say_white_full)


# Combine everything into one table
efficacy_threeway_results <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  care_black_threeway,
  care_white_threeway,
  say_black_threeway,
  say_white_threeway
) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(outcome, race, year)
```

```{r Step 4: Predicted Value Plots, include=TRUE}
get_efficacy_predictions <- function(model_list) {
  
  results <- lapply(model_list, function(x) {
    
    if (is.null(x)) return(NULL)
    
    # Get the factor levels actually used by this model
    model_data <- model.frame(x$model)
    
    finance_levels <- levels(
      model_data$personal_finances_scale_factor
    )
    
    income_levels <- levels(
      model_data$income_group_factor
    )
    
    # Prediction grid using only estimable factor levels
    newdata <- expand.grid(
      personal_finances_scale_factor = finance_levels,
      income_group_factor = income_levels,
      stock_owns = c(0, 1)
    )
    
    # Make sure the newdata variables have the same factor levels
    # as those used to estimate the model
    newdata$personal_finances_scale_factor <- factor(
      newdata$personal_finances_scale_factor,
      levels = finance_levels
    )
    
    newdata$income_group_factor <- factor(
      newdata$income_group_factor,
      levels = income_levels
    )
    
    # Predicted values
    newdata$predicted <- as.numeric(
      predict(
        x$model,
        newdata = newdata,
        type = "response"
      )
    )
    
    # Metadata
    newdata$year <- x$year
    newdata$race <- x$race
    newdata$outcome <- x$outcome
    newdata$n <- x$n
    
    newdata
  })
  
  dplyr::bind_rows(results)
}
```
